newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says Iran poisoned 85 Iranian Kurds.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says Iran poisoned 85 Iranian Kurds.

text.p: An Iraqi official said on Sunday 85 Iranian Kurdish dissidents were being treated in Baghdad hospitals for poisoning and accused Tehran of contaminating their food with the highly toxic metal thallium.

Health ministry undersecretary Shawky Marcus said many of those poisoned, who belong to the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran (KDPI), were in critical condition and Baghdad was trying to arrange their transfer to Europe for better care.
The KDPI, whose forces are based in rebel-controlled northern Iraq, has also accused Iranian agents of slipping thallium into their food and water.
"The number we (have) received until today in Saddam Medical City is 26 and in Karama hospital is 59," Marcus told reporters.
"From the history we took from these patients...they get food which is polluted by thallium which is the most dangerious poison," he said.
He said Iraq, as a result of U.N. sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait, lacked the medical supplies necessary to treat those in critical condition.
"We are in the process of informing international organisations to help even for the management of some critical cases outside Iraq, in Europe," he added.
Marcus accused Iran of poisoning the KDPI members. "The Iranian regime...their attitude is in favour of such behaviour," he said.
Iraq and Iran fought a ruinous war from 1980 to 1988. Despite a U.N.-brokered ceasefire, the two countries are still at loggerheads over soldiers missing in action, prisoners of war and other issues.
